keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 39,178 km2 (141 cells), Kalimantan Tengah and only 34 percent of Kalimantan Selatan; the page says Banjar once controlled all of South Kalimantan, most of Central Kalimantan, and a ring of tributaries (Kotawaringin, Sukadana, Sintang, Sanggau, Sekadau, Melawi, Landak, southern and western Sambas, Paser, Kutai, Berau, Tawau and the Sulu archipelago), all of which paid tribute. No year, no area. I add all of South Kalimantan to the shape and leave the tribute zone out; the shape applies 1526-1858.

The Cliopatria row ends in 1859, the page has the Dutch dissolve the sultanate in 1860 (the body text typo reads '1960') and the Banjarmasin War page that the Dutch 'abolished the Sultanate of Bandjermasin in its entirety' after Tamjid's abdication in June 1859: the shape applies 1859-1860.

region.text: Banjarmasin on the Barito delta (Kuin) and the Banjar lowlands

ledger.note: 1526: Raden Samudra becomes Sultan Surianshah. The body text has him converting to Islam on 24 September 1526 and taking the name Sultan Surianshah, with help from Mangkubumi Aria Taranggana; the infobox dates the kingdom 1520-1905 and the first sovereign 1520-1540. The page gives the capital (Kuin), not the first boundary; the Demak help is for the Negara Daha war, whose year is not on the page.
1612: the capital moves from Kuin to Pamakuan (infobox 'Pamakuan (1612-1622)').
1622: the capital moves to Muara Tambangan; the page adds that Sultan Agung of Mataram planned to colonise Banjar-held areas in 1622 but cancelled the plan for lack of resources.
1632: the capital moves to Batang Banyu (infobox 1632-1642); the VOC's attack on Banjarmasin failed in 1633.
1642: the capital moves to Old Martapura (infobox 1642-1663).
1663: the capital moves to Banjarmasin and Batang Alai (infobox lists both for 1663-1679/80); in 1660-1663 a peace treaty was made with the Dutch under Rakyatullah.
1680: the capital moves to Kayu Tangi, after Tahlilullah, backed by the Dutch, won the invasion of Banjar in 1679.
1857: the Dutch install Tamjidillah II and the court is at Banjarmasin again (infobox 1857-1860); the installation triggers the Banjar War.

region.text: the Banjar heartland: Banjarmasin, Pengaron, Martapura, Tanah Laut and the Barito

ledger.note: 1859: the Banjarmasin War breaks out. 'On 1 May 1859, all the Europeans at the Julia Hermina coal mine at Kalangan were murdered'; the Dutch commander 'on 29 April 1859 assumed military command at Bandjermasin'; 'At the end of 1859 the battlefield was spread across 3 locations', around Martapura, Tanah Laut and along the Barito River.

1860: the Dutch dissolve the sultanate. The Banjar page has the Dutch dissolving it in 1860 (body text typo '1960'); Hidayatullah II, sultan 1859-1862, 'surrendered himself to the Dutch in early 1862'; Antasari died on 11 October 1862; 'The war ended with a Dutch victory in 1863' and fighting went on at Baras Kuning until 1905. The contest is ended here with the dissolution; the rebels' hold on the countryside to 1863 is not mapped.

region.text: the whole sultanate, annexed to the Dutch East Indies

ledger.note: 1860: the Dutch abolish the Sultanate of Banjar. The Dutch dissolved the sultanate; Cliopatria's Banjar row ends in 1859 and its Dutch East Indies 1860 shape contains all of it. The infobox keeps a sovereign (Muhammad Seman, 1862-1905) in resistance, and annexation into the Dutch East Indies in 1905.

wars.name: Dutch East India Company attack on Banjarmasin
wars.outcome: A failed VOC attack on Banjarmasin; a peace treaty followed in 1660-1663 under Rakyatullah.

wars.name: Banjar civil war of 1679
wars.outcome: Tahlilullah, backed by the Dutch, won the invasion of Banjar and gave the VOC more economic authority.
wars.note: No territorial result. In 1757 Prince Amir, backed by Bugis forces, attacked and the VOC under Captain Hoffman defeated him; in 1787 Amir was exiled to Sri Lanka and 'Banjar became a Dutch protectorate' (the page also dates protectorate status to Adam's reign, 1825-1857): a vassal_start for the dutch-republic (eu-09) or Dutch East Indies (se-03) dossiers.

wars.name: Banjarmasin War

zones.text: Banjarmasin, Pengaron, Martapura, Tanah Laut, the Barito

wars.outcome: Dutch victory in 1863 after the abolition of the sultanate in 1860, sporadic fighting to 1905. Rebel-held land: Demang Lehman took the Tabanio fort in Tanah Laut in August 1859 and attacked Amawang on 31 March 1860.
wars.note: The Banjar page's infobox gives 1859-1906, the war page 1859-1863. Rebel territory is not mapped on either page.

certainty.note: A river-and-delta state with a tribute ring; no survey or treaty line anywhere in the pages opened.

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Neither gives an area, so Cliopatria's 39,178 km2 could not be compared.
DISAGREEMENTS: the Cliopatria row ends in 1859; the Banjar page has the Dutch dissolve the sultanate in 1860 (text typo '1960') and the war page puts the abolition after Tamjid's June 1859 abdication; the war ends in 1863 (war page) or 1906 (Banjar infobox); the founding is 1520 (infobox, reign start) or 1526 (conversion on 24 September 1526).
PAGE SILENT: the dates of Surianshah's conquest of Negara Daha and Demak's help; Banjar's tribute ring (Kotawaringin to Sulu) is undated, so no vassal events are written; the rebels' hold on the countryside 1860-1863; the date of the Dutch protectorate (1787 on the Banjar page); the capital sites (placed in the Banjar heartland).
NEEDS DOSSIERS: Negara Daha (predecessor); the Banjar resistance 1860-1905 (Hidayatullah II, Antasari, Muhammad Seman at Baras Kuning), a rebel state if a source maps its land; the Dutch dossiers should carry the 1787 protectorate as vassal_start with counterpart sultanate-of-banjar.
